item.title: France's famed Bordeaux wine country has been charred by wildfire
item.description: Southwest France has seen wildfires in the past. But the fires that raged last week and scorched 100,000 acres are something new to the region.

item.title: Phoenix sears under sweltering heat
item.description: Much of the western U-S is facing dangerously high temperatures this weekend. Phoenix is expecting highs above 110 degrees. And public cooling centers are seeing high demand.

item.description: An avid fly fisherman in Vermont shares his love of the craft and how its shaped his mental health journey.

item.title: Viral 'Teen Takeover' trend is causing trouble in some communities
item.description: Communities across the country are dealing with "Teen Takeovers" this summer. The viral social media trend is causing disruptions in public spaces across the country. Teens in Charlotte weigh in.

item.title: Police shooting in Madison, Wis. sparks renewed calls for officers to wear body cams
item.description: Police in Madison, Wisconsin don't widely use body cameras. That policy is under renewed scrutiny following the recent shooting death of a 38-year-old Black man at the hands of police.

item.title: How Switzerland became the nuclear bomb shelter capital of the world
item.description: Switzerland is home to over 370,000 nuclear bomb shelters. The historically neutral nation guarantees each of its 9 million citizens a spot in case of an emergency.

item.title: How the 1972 Polaroid SX-70 revolutionized consumer photography
item.description: In 1972, the Polaroid SX-70, made in collaboration with a famous industrial designer named Henry Dreyfuss, was a revelation. The object is on view at the Cooper Hewitt Smithsonian museum of design in New York City.
